hosting.//: SPA fallback: any path that is not a real file is served index.html so /product/:id deep links resolve client-side.

headers.//: Placeholder SVGs are not content-hashed, so keep them on a short cache.
Vite emits content-hashed filenames here — safe to cache forever.
Baseline security headers applied to every response.

Firebase Auth needs several external origins allowed. script-src: the redirect flow injects https://apis.google.com/js/api.js. connect-src: identitytoolkit (auth API), securetoken (token exchange), plus accounts.google.com which the SDK probes for FedCM support. frame-src: the __/auth/iframe hosted on the project's authDomain. img-src: Google avatar hosts. 'unsafe-inline' is still required for React inline style attributes.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com https://*.googleusercontent.com; font-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://apis.google.com; connect-src 'self' https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com https://www.googleapis.com https://firebaseinstallations.googleapis.com https://content-firebaseappcheck.googleapis.com https://accounts.google.com; frame-src https://accounts.google.com https://*.firebaseapp.com https://*.web.app; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.//: Everything that is NOT a built asset — i.e. the HTML shell, whether requested as '/', '/index.html' or a rewritten SPA route such as '/product/sm-ph-01'. Firebase otherwise defaults HTML documents to max-age=3600, which is unsafe here: after a deploy the content-hashed bundle referenced by a cached shell is gone and clients get a white screen. This rule uses a negated glob so it must stay AFTER the /assets rules above, which win for static files.
